messages:
Alex Chen: pushing a quick proposal — add a per-model 'hotpath econ' card to the cost dashboard that shows token-level cost, cache savings, and effective unit cost, broken down by route and model variant. mock: https://figma.redwood/proto/econ-hotpath :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Priya Nair: good idea. main Q: do we show raw cache credits or the amortized savings? enterprises will want both, but raw can confuse teams that use shared caches
Mateo Ruiz: my 2c: surface the amortized savings in the default view, raw credits behind a quick toggle. less noise for 90% users, power users can dig in
Dani Park: also need to consider sampling overhead. token-level telemetry at 100% increases backend cost. we should support adaptive sampling + estimate correction
Alex Chen: agreed. proposal: default sample_rate=0.05 for token traces, with an SDK-side correction multiplier and a UI confidence band. link to sampling writeup: https://docs.internal/sampling-econ
Casey Li: how does this affect our API shape? do we add a new /metrics/econ endpoint or extend /metrics/usage? want to avoid breaking existing dashboard consumers
Mateo Ruiz: add new endpoint /v1/metrics/econ that returns aggregated rows with fields: model, route, tokens_charged, tokens_saved_cache, effective_token_cost_usd, sample_rate, confidence_interval. keeps it explicit
Dani Park: we must be careful about exposing per-tenant raw per-invocation traces to self-serve consoles. for private deployments this is fine, but hosted customers may require masking/rollup to org-level only
Alex Chen: good point. implement role-based visibility: operators & billing team can see tenant-level; customer-facing console shows only tenant-aggregates and anonymized samples. also add opt-out for sensitive accounts
Priya Nair: UX: the card should show 3 KPIs up top (avg effective cost, pct cache saving, tokens/sec) and an expandable line item table below for models/variants. include a 'what changed' diff for rollouts
Casey Li: rollout plan idea: feature-flag the card off by default, enable for internal + canary orgs, then 10% of orgs after 2 weeks. use server-side flag so we can flip back quickly if telemetry cost spikes
Alex Chen: sample API snippet for engineering to wire up:
```
GET /internal/v1/metrics/econ?start=2026-03-01T00:00Z&end=2026-03-07T00:00Z&group_by=model,route&sample=0.05
Response: [{"model":"redwood-1.5","route":"/chat","tokens_charged":1234567,"tokens_saved_cache":234567,"effective_token_cost_usd":"0.000012","sample_rate":0.05}]
```
Priya Nair: love the confidence band idea. we should show a heck/low/high in UI and a tooltip explaining sampling correction and noise
Mateo Ruiz: one technical nit: cache savings attribution for prefix-sharing routes is tricky. need lineage mapping so we don't double-count shared prefixes across tenants or routes
Dani Park: agrees. we can emit a cache_fingerprint and lineage_id in the backend metrics so the attributor can collapse duplicates. but that increases cardinality — another reason to rely on sampling + bloom filters
Casey Li: from infra side: add a hard cap on token telemetry ingestion per org to avoid noisy customers burning our metrics pipeline. cap=5M traces/day per org by default, adjustable with a support request
Alex Chen: next steps: Dani + Mateo to spec the backend fields and sampling math, Priya to mock the card and tooltip copy, Casey to add the feature flag gating + ingestion caps, I'll draft a short RFC for the API and rollout timeline
infra-bot: deploy-canary initiated for feature-flag "econ-hotpath-card" on cluster-us-east-2 — build 2026.3.227: success :rocket:
Priya Nair: thanks — I'll add copy for the 'why this matters' microcopy and a sample demo dataset for product review
Alex Chen: sweet. tagging @billing for FYI on metric names and invoice mapping
Mateo Ruiz: tagging internal ops to watch for telemetry spike after canary. I'll add alerts for ingestion > 120% baseline.
